jobs.title: Marketing Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/03/2026 Marketing Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the marketing team and touches everything: what we publish, what we spend, and whether the growth engine actually compounds. Read the whole post before applying.This is not make-a-mood-board-and-watch. You'll be publishing real content under our name, running real campaigns with real budgets behind them, and owning numbers that leadership actually looks at. Real deadlines, real consequences, with the Marketing Manager beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the marketing engine actually works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doContent and channelsWrite across everything we publish: blog posts, emails, landing pages, social content, campaign copy. What you write goes live.Support SEO research, format and optimize blog content, and build and maintain website pages.Schedule and publish across our social channels, then track what performs and say why.Engage physician conversations across forums, social platforms, and the communities where our audience already spends time. You'll be speaking as the firm, so precision matters.Build graphics and marketing assets to support campaigns across channels.Campaigns and operationsEmail: build and proof campaigns before they go out, manage list segmentation, and catch the typo before ten thousand physicians see it.Paid media: support campaign assets, pull performance data, and track results against goals.Partnerships: track deliverables across partner programs and keep co-branded content moving. Nobody chases you; you chase them.Events and webinars: promotional assets, registration pages, post-event follow-up.Analytics: keep tracking and attribution clean, build regular performance reports, and dig into what's working and what isn't. When a number looks wrong, find out why before someone asks.Research: track competitors and market trends, and surface what's worth acting on.Growth projects: help launch channels and platforms we don't have yet.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Writing. You write clean, tight copy that doesn't need a rewrite before it ships. You know the difference between words that fill space and words that move someone. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Detail. Marketing looks polished or sloppy based entirely on the small things: the broken link, the wrong UTM, the subject line that renders badly on mobile. You catch these before they go out, not after.Numbers and follow-through. You think in steps and notice when something doesn't add up. A campaign's attribution is off, a partner deliverable is nine days late, two reports disagree on last month's leads. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And be honest with yourself about the manual work. A lot of this is scheduling, formatting, data cleanup, and tracking spreadsheets. It is not always interesting. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If tedious-but-important work drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: anything carrying real brand or spend exposure (budget decisions, public statements on tax positions, partner commitments) is yours to prepare and the Marketing Manager's to decide. Be ready to prove it.Organized, accurate, fast. Comfortable in spreadsheets and picking up new tools and platforms quickly.Familiar with marketing channels and how they connect to each other.Curious about a niche industry. Physician tax is more interesting than it sounds.Prior marketing experience is a plus: an internship, a class project, a club, or something you built yourself.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

WHAT YOU’LL BRINGRecent graduates (ideally within the past 12 months) and/or individuals pursuing Master’s degrees in the physical sciences or science communications.Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail. Demonstrated interest in science, research, and science communication. Ability to research complex topics and communicate them clearly to broad audiences. Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines. Ability to collaborate effectively with a team while working independently on assigned projects. Experience in journalism, communications, or science writing is preferred but not required. TO APPLY: Include a resume and a cover letter. We encourage you to apply even if your experience does not fully match the position description. At AIP, we embrace considering people from a diversity of backgrounds and career experiences. COMPENSATION: $18.80 - $19.20 per hour WORKING AT AIP: AIP embraces a flexible hybrid work environment to balance in-person collaborative work with remote work. The team works in a flexible, hybrid schedule and reports to our offices in College Park, Maryland and Washington, DC, as needed. Employees are required to reside in the DC Metro regions of Maryland, Virginia, or Washington, DC. Your colleagues at AIP are welcoming, gracious, and eager to help each other succeed. With our commitment to community service, institute-wide social opportunities, and ongoing learning and development, AIP is a rewarding place to work. ABOUT AIP: Scientific discovery shapes our lives every day. And AIP empowers the organizations and people that make those discoveries possible.As a Federation, AIP advances the success of a community of more than 30 independent scientific organizations. They, in turn, support hundreds of thousands of professionals across many scientific and engineering disciplines. AIP creates shared spaces — forums, conversations, connections — where individual action among our Member Organizations becomes collective impact.As an Institute, AIP preserves the history of discovery so the past can guide the future. jobs.title: Investment Intern at Public School & Education Employees Retirement Systems of Missouri
jobs.description: Employer: Public School & Education Employees Retirement Systems of Missouri Expires: 09/03/2026 Join the Summer 2027 Investment Intern team at Missouri’s largest defined benefit pension plan, where you’ll play a meaningful role in supporting a high-performing institutional investment program that serves educators across the state. This internship offers the opportunity to contribute to work that strengthens the long-term financial security of Missouri’s public education employees while gaining exposure to multiple asset classes and the daily operations of a world-class investment department. We are seeking motivated, detail-oriented students who are ready to learn, take initiative, and collaborate with our Chief Financial Officer and Investment Staff on a wide range of analytical projects, operational tasks, and investment research. Salary: $25.00/hour Job Type: Internship Location: Jefferson City, Missouri About PSRS/PEERSPSRS/PEERS is the largest defined benefit pension plan in the state of Missouri, proudly serving over 320,000 members. In partnership with Missouri’s public-school districts, we are committed to providing secure and reliable retirement benefits to the state’s dedicated educators and education employees. Our Investments team operates from our newly remodeled and expanded headquarters in Jefferson City, Missouri. Designed with both innovation and comfort in mind, our facility features state-of-the-art technology, advanced security, ergonomic workspaces, and collaborative areas that foster teamwork and productivity. We also maintain an office in St. Louis, Missouri, providing additional support and resources for staff and members throughout the state. About the JobAs an Investment Intern, you will be immersed in a sophisticated, world-class institutional investment program responsible for approximately $65 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025. The investment program is designed to achieve an annual return of at least 7.3% over long periods of time through a thoughtfully diversified portfolio that spans public and private markets in both domestic and international regions. In this role, you will work closely with the Chief Financial Officer, the Investment Operations Manager, and Senior Portfolio Managers, gaining hands‑on experience across public equity, private credit, real estate, and hedged strategies. This position reports directly to the Investment Operations Manager and indirectly to one or more Senior Portfolio Managers, providing a structured and collaborative environment for learning and professional growth. Your work will support a range of analytical and operational activities, including investment research, data analysis, reporting, and special projects essential to the daily functioning of the investment program. This paid internship offers flexible scheduling, a professional learning environment, and meaningful opportunities to contribute to a high-performing investment team while building a strong foundation for a future career in finance or investments. Job RequirementsOur ideal candidate is a student entering or enrolled in college and pursuing a bachelor’s degree or master’s degree in business administration, finance, accounting, economics or a related field. A student with a strong desire to earn the Charter Financial Analyst (CFA) is preferred. The Investment Intern should bring intellectual curiosity, professionalism, and a collaborative mindset, working effectively both independently and as part of a team while building positive relationships across the department. Candidates must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication skills, a solid understanding of finance and investment concepts, familiarity with financial analysis methods, and the ability to support key administrative processes. Success in this role requires the ability to prepare clear reports and presentations, maintain organized physical and electronic files, and use standard business software proficiently, including Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with databases is also beneficial and supports the technical aspects of the position.

jobs.description: Employer: Medtronic Expires: 09/03/2026 CAREERS THAT CHANGE LIVES The possibilities at the intersection of medicine and technology are endless, which means endless opportunities to make your mark on the world. Supply Chain: Integrates demand planning, procurement, manufacturing, logistics, and continuous improvement to drive cost efficiency, regulatory compliance, resiliency, and service performance across Medtronic’s global business units. Plans, sources, manufactures, and distributes medical technologies worldwide, ensuring high-quality products reach hospitals, clinicians, and patients safely, reliably, and on time. Supply Management: Identifies, selects, and manages suppliers to ensure a reliable, cost-effective, and high-quality supply of materials, components, and services that support patient therapies worldwide. Drives supplier performance, mitigates supply risks, ensures regulatory and quality compliance, and delivers cost savings through contract management, supplier development, and strategic procurement initiatives. Location and Work Model The majority of internship positions are based at primary hubs in Minnesota with additional opportunities available in Colorado, Connecticut, Tennessee, and Texas. Candidate location preferences are strongly considered during the interview and offer process; however, flexibility increases the number of potential opportunities available. All interns must reside in the U.S. for the duration of the internship. Medtronic is working a minimum of 4 days a week onsite as part of its commitment to professional growth, cross-functional collaboration, and engineering the extraordinary. Must Have: Minimum Requirements To be considered for a Summer 2027 Supply Chain/Supply Management internship, your resume must clearly demonstrate how you meet each of these basic requirements. Working toward a bachelor’s in Supply Chain Management or a related major with an anticipated graduation date of Winter 2027, Spring 2028, Winter 2028, or Spring 2029. Ability to participate full time, 40 hours per week, as part of the intern cohort from June 1-August 13 for semester system programs or June 14-August 20 for quarter system programs. About Medtronic: Together, as one of the largest medical device companies in the country, we can change healthcare worldwide. At Medtronic, we push the limits of what technology, therapies, and services can do to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Help us shape the future and engineer the extraordinary. You'll be building dashboards, automations, and analyses that real teams use to make real decisions in real time. The feedback loop is short, the stakes are real, and the impact is visible.You'll work at the center of culture, not adjacent to it - 11:11 Media sits at the intersection of entertainment, commerce, fashion, beauty, and wellness. jobs.title: 2027 Procurement Internship at Nestlé
jobs.description: Employer: Nestlé Expires: 09/05/2026 2027 Procurement InternshipFoods you love. Brands you trust. And a career that empowers you to grow. At Nestlé USA, we’re all working towards the same goal – to delight and deliver for our consumers. With a rich portfolio of beloved brands, including DiGiorno, Toll House, and Coffee mate, in 97% of U.S. households, we have a unique opportunity – and responsibility – to be there for every moment in our consumers’ lives. Joining Nestlé means becoming part of an inclusive workplace that inspires innovation, encourages strategic thinking and creativity, and celebrates your achievements. No matter where you work within the organization, you are empowered to challenge the status quo, embrace risk-taking, and pioneer new ideas. Our supportive and collaborative environment encourages bold ambitions and continuous learning so that everyone can grow and thrive. This position is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship. Here’s a breakdown of the 2027 Nestlé USA Procurement Internship Program: At Nestlé USA, our Procurement team is driven by the desire to be a competitive advantage to the businesses that we support. Inspired by our company’s 4 Ways of Winning – Speed, Agility, Collaboration, and Courage – Nestlé’s Procurement professionals strive to deliver value efficiently and effectively, strategically manage our Direct and Indirect spend categories, and ensure supply to fulfill our commitments to deliver outstanding value to our customers and consumer. Nestlé offers a 10-week internship program designed to provide you with the experience and knowledge essential for a successful career within Procurement. This internship is project-based, allowing you to take ownership of a project from start to finish, addressing a critical gap within the function and driving tangible value for the business. Through comprehensive, hands-on, and strategically integrated opportunities, this program aims to develop well-balanced Procurement professionals. Location: Roles are based in a corporate office location in Solon, OH or Arlington, VA. Must be flexible to work remote or in the office on any given day and reside within a commutable distance to Solon, OH or Arlington, VA. Education Requirements: Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Procurement, Supply Chain, Business, Operations Management or other related field is required. Degree completed by June 2028 Preferred Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above. Experience Requirements: Preferred Procurement or related internship/co-op experience. Additional Requirements: You should be available to start the program in June 2027. We're looking for passionate individuals who thrive on working on diverse business projects that involve research, cost analyses, and engaging stakeholders. Show us your drive and determination. You should be a collaborative team player who excels in working with others. Strong communication, influence, leadership, and analytical skills are essential. We want to see you make a difference in our organization. Experience working with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Word and Excel, is preferred. Perks: Competitive compensation. Gain firsthand corporate experience in Procurement. It's your chance to immerse yourself in the professional world and make meaningful impacts. Contributing member of the team, accountable for results and project deliverables. Direct exposure to foundational Procurement principles. Work with an influential industry leader in consumer-packaged goods (Fortune Magazine) and top 5 Supply Chain organizations as ranked by Gartner. Work in a dynamic and collaborative culture. Opportunity to network with Nestlé employees globally. Successful completion of internship could lead to full-time Employment opportunities with Nestlé Procurement (Nestlé Procurement Development Program). jobs.description: Employer: Presto Expires: 09/05/2026 About PrestoPresto is the leading Voice AI company for restaurant drive-thrus, operating at scale in complex, noisy, customer-facing environments. As the AI partner to more than a dozen of the most iconic American restaurant brands, Presto is building one of the most impactful real-world applications of AI that directly impacts revenue, labor efficiency, and a magical guest experience for millions of people.AI is not a feature at Presto; it is the foundation of how we build, evaluate, and evolve our products. We operate at lightning-speed iteration cycles and are solving some of the hardest problems in Voice AI. We are backed by Remus Capital, were a Y Combinator company, and are headquartered in Silicon Valley.This may not be the right fit for you if you are looking for a traditional 9-to-5 environment. We move at the pace of AI. Change is constant, and roadmaps evolve quickly. Presto is for builders, experimenters, and problem-solvers who thrive in ambiguity, learn continuously, and are excited to shape the future of real-world AI alongside a high-performance team.The OpportunityPresto is partnering with universities across the U.S. to place a select group of students inside restaurants where our AI system is already live.This internship sits at the intersection of technology, business, and operations. You’ll play a critical role in helping us understand how our AI performs in real-world environments, analyzing interactions, identifying trends, and uncovering opportunities to improve both customer experience and business outcomes.The candidate must be located in Raleigh, NC or Southern California or San Francisco, CA or Stockton, CA. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Sales Intern (BDR) at Fastflo
jobs.description: Employer: Fastflo Expires: 09/05/2026 Sales Intern (BRD)Fastflo | Remote | Part-time or Full-time | Base + CommissionAbout FastfloFastflo is a VC-backed B2B SaaS startup built at the Harvard Innovation Labs. We're changing how companies hire frontline workers: instead of forcing candidates through clunky web forms, applications happen natively inside iMessage and other messaging apps. The result is that around 80% of candidates finish their application, versus roughly 15% on traditional flows. We recently closed our seed round and count global enterprise brands and multi-location franchise operators among our customers.We're now scaling our sales pipeline, and that's where you come in.The RoleYou will own the very top of our sales engine. We hand you qualified lead lists; your job is to get decision makers on the phone and book meetings for our closing team. You are not selling on these calls, and you're not expected to. Your single goal is simple and measurable: turn a qualified lead into a booked meeting. Our team takes it from there and closes the deal.This is the fastest possible education in startup sales. You'll learn how to open a cold call, handle a brush-off, earn thirty seconds of attention from a busy operator, and convert it into a calendar invite. These are skills that compound for the rest of your career, and you'll build them with direct coaching from our founder and sales leadership, not from the back row of a large sales floor.Booking meetings is where you start, not where you stop. Prove yourself on the phones and your scope grows with you: sitting in on the sales calls you booked, running parts of discovery and demos, and taking on responsibilities across the sales cycle and the wider business. At a startup this size, the people who deliver get handed more, quickly.What You'll DoCold call decision makers from qualified lead lists we provideBook discovery meetings for the closing team and hand off clean contextTrack your outreach and results in our CRMRefine call scripts and openers with the team based on what's actually workingGet direct visibility into how booked meetings turn into closed dealsWhat Success Looks LikeQualified meetings booked. That's the metric. You'll have a clear weekly target, full transparency on your numbers, and commission tied directly to the meetings you put on the calendar.Who Thrives HereCurrently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor's or master's degreeComfortable picking up the phone and talking to strangers, or genuinely eager to become comfortable fastResilient: you can hear "no" ten times and dial the eleventh number with energyCoachable, organized, and self-directed in a remote environmentNo prior sales experience required. We provide training, scripts, and ongoing coaching.Compensation & LogisticsBase pay (hourly) plus commissionAcademic credit available where your program allows, in addition to compensationFully remotePart-time or full-time depending on your availabilityStrong performers have a clear path to a Summer 2026 internship or a full-time role

jobs.title: 2027 Portfolio Management & Investment Research Summer Analyst at StepStone Group LP
jobs.description: Employer: StepStone Group LP Expires: 09/06/2026 We are global private markets specialists delivering tailored investment solutions, advisory services, and impactful, data driven insights to the world’s investors. Leveraging the power of our platform and our peerless intelligence across sectors, strategies, and geographies, we help identify the advantages and the answers our clients need to succeed.The team you’ll joinThe Portfolio Management team at StepStone serves as a central resource for the firm's evergreen fund client base, wearing multiple hats across portfolio construction, investment decision-making, and commitment pacing. The team works directly with clients of StepStone's evergreen accounts to build and maintain portfolios across private markets, fielding pacing requests and translating investment strategy into actionable allocation decisions. Leveraging StepStone's proprietary data advantage, the team applies quantitative rigor to help the firm make informed investment decisions across asset classes - from buyouts and secondaries to real assets and beyond. The team also supports valuation work spanning multiple private market asset classes, ensuring analytical consistency and accuracy across the platform. Beyond core portfolio and investment responsibilities, the team plays a key role in automating and enhancing firmwide workflows, developing Python and Excel-based tools that drive efficiency and create lasting operational value across the organization.About the roleStepStone is currently seeking candidates with strong analytical, coding, and business acumen for intern positions within the Portfolio Management team. This internship is ideal for candidates with a background in finance, economics, or related fields who also possess solid programming skills. Interns will gain hands-on experience in portfolio management, investment research, and data-driven decision-making in private markets.At StepStone, we value a team-first approach, a low-ego mindset, and intellectual curiosity. We are looking for candidates who are eager to learn, take ownership of their work, and contribute to a highly collaborative environment.What you’ll doSummer Analysts will contribute directly to the Portfolio Management team's core workflows, supporting portfolio construction, quantitative modeling, valuation and data-driven research across private markets. Summer Analysts may also help develop and test key Python and Excel tools used in active portfolio decision-making. Throughout the summer, Summer Analysts will also have the opportunity to contribute to research projects that identify trends in private markets and communicate findings to internal teams.Key ResponsibilitiesWork with private markets data, collecting and reconciling information from internal sources (MySQL, PDFs and Excel files)Develop and test financial models to support investment decision-making (Python, R, VBA, Power Query).Conduct data-driven analyses to identify trends in private markets.Support portfolio management efforts through ad hoc analysis and research projects.Communicate insights and findings to internal teams and produce written documentation of data, models, and code.What we’re looking forPursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Analytics, or a related field.Undergraduate student graduating anywhere from December 2027 through June 2028.Previous internship or work experience in finance, consulting, or data analysis is strongly preferred.Solid understanding of Python, R, or VBA for data analysis.Familiarity with financial markets, investment concepts, and private markets is a plus.Strong attention to detail and ability to critically check work while maintaining a humble, learning-focused approach.Team-oriented mindset—able to take feedback constructively, collaborate effectively, and contribute to shared goals.Proficiency in Excel; experience with SQL, Power BI, or data visualization tools is a plus.No task is too small—willingness to roll up sleeves and take initiative in a fast-paced environmentWhy join us?At StepStone, we foster a supportive and inclusive team culture where collaboration and learning are the core of what we do. Our collegial atmosphere encourages teamwork, mentorship, and professional development. This summer internship is a great opportunity to gain practical experience and develop critical skills that will help you launch a successful career in Private Markets. Click here to learn more about the intern experience.Salary: $30 / hour

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Program Intern at International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition
jobs.description: Employer: International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition Expires: 09/06/2026 About the IACCFounded more than 40 years ago, the International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition (IACC) is the world’s oldest and largest organization devoted exclusively to representing the interests of companies concerned with trademark counterfeiting, piracy, and the related theft of intellectual property. The IACC comprises approximately 250 companies, trade associations, and professional firms. Its members include many of the world’s best-known brands across a broad range of industries, including luxury goods and apparel, automotive, consumer goods, entertainment, pharmaceuticals, and other product sectors. We are a lean and highly operational organization and a leading voice for companies addressing counterfeiting issues. Through advocacy, law enforcement training, events, strategic partnerships, and collaborative programs at the national and international levels, we build partnerships and develop creative solutions to combat the growing problem of intellectual property theft around the world. Position DescriptionThe IACC is seeking an energetic, team-oriented, and motivated student to join our team as a part-time Program Intern. The Program Intern will provide hands-on support for the IACC’s online intellectual property (IP) enforcement programs. The intern will assist companies of all sizes with enforcing their IP rights on international e-commerce platforms by supporting the processing of infringement complaints, maintaining program data, communicating with program participants, and providing Chinese-language support. This internship is designed for a currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student interested in intellectual property, international business, e-commerce, or program operations. The intern will have the opportunity to gain practical experience working with international companies, online platforms, and intellectual property enforcement programs. ResponsibilitiesThe Program Intern will work under the supervision of a designated program supervisor. Responsibilities may include:Process participant submissions: Review participant submissions and ensure they are made in accordance with operational guidelines. Process complaints and disputed claims in accordance with program protocols. Track relevant deadlines and participants’ responses. Effectively communicate with English-speaking participants on operational issues related to submissions. Report and escalate issues to the program supervisor.Data entry and translation: Collect data, provide translation from Chinese to English, and update information in the program portal to ensure timely reporting to participants. Process data accurately and efficiently. Report trends to the program supervisor. Track key data points as directed.Participant communication and engagement: Guide participants on the submission process as needed. Respond to operational questions and communicate with participants as needed to ensure a positive program experience. Skills Required: Fluency in both English and Mandarin Chinese Preferred: Familiarity with data-tracking and information-processing toolsInterest in or knowledge of intellectual property Education and Experience Required: Current enrollment in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program Preferred: Previous internship, part-time work, volunteer, or student organization experienceExperience in program administration or operational supportExperience in customer service or participant engagement Location and Start DateThis position is based in Washington, DC, with a hybrid work arrangement that includes both in-office and remote work. The anticipated start date is late August 2026. Expected Hours and PayThis is a part-time, hourly, non-exempt position requiring approximately 20 hours per week, with compensation of $18.50–$20.00 per hour and a schedule to be established in coordination with the selected candidate. The internship may also be eligible for academic credit, subject to the requirements and approval of the selected candidate’s college or university. Other InformationThe International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status. Application InstructionsPlease send a resume, cover letter, and one writing sample to marketsafeinfo@iacc.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

jobs.title: Bilingual Market Explorer Intern – Home Backup Energy at Renogy
jobs.description: Employer: Renogy Expires: 09/06/2026 Bilingual Market Explorer Intern – Home Backup Energy Location: Texas-basedWork arrangement: This is a hybrid, Texas-based field internship. Interns may complete internal meetings, planning, and reporting remotely; however, regular in-person fieldwork is required in one or more of Renogy’s priority Texas markets: Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Austin, and San Antonio.Employment Type: Paid Internship, Part-Time (20–30 hours/week)Duration: 12 weeksCompensation: Hourly pay, commensurate with experience; approved local travel and field expenses reimbursedPotential for Conversion: High-performing interns may be considered for a full-time Associate Market Development role. About the RoleRenogy is seeking two curious, proactive, and bilingual interns to help us understand the real-world need for home backup energy solutions in Texas.This is not a traditional desk-based marketing internship. You will conduct field research with homeowners, communities, electricians, HVAC providers, solar installers, and local partners. Your work will help identify customer needs, purchase barriers, product opportunities, and local go-to-market strategies for home backup power solutions.We are hiring for two complementary focus areas. Candidates may be matched based on their background and strengths. Focus Area 1: Consumer & Community Market ExplorerInterview homeowners who have experienced power outages to understand their needs, priorities, budgets, and decision-making process.Participate in community outreach, homeowner discussions, and product demonstrations.Assist with home energy-load assessments and backup-power solution testing.Gather customer feedback on product capacity, runtime, pricing, installation, and brand trust.Help develop local customer insights and case studies for the Texas market. Focus Area 2: Installer & Ecosystem Market ExplorerConduct outreach to local electricians, HVAC companies, solar installers, home-improvement businesses, and other relevant partners.Participate in field visits and home-site assessments when appropriate.Learn about installation workflows, labor requirements, pricing, margins, and partnership needs.Help identify and qualify potential local installation and channel partners.Build and maintain a local target-account and partner database. What You’ll DoConduct customer and partner interviews, both in person and remotely.Perform outreach via phone, email, and in-person visits.Document evidence, insights, objections, and recommendations from field work.Support small-scale market experiments and evaluate results.Work with Renogy’s U.S. market, product, engineering, and operations teams.Submit a weekly Evidence & Decision Memo summarizing findings, changed assumptions, and proposed next steps. QualificationsStrong English communication skills, including the ability to independently conduct interviews and outreach; Mandarin Chinese proficiency is preferred because the role involves collaboration with Renogy product and engineering teams in China.Comfortable with cold calling, in-person outreach, and speaking with homeowners and business owners.Curious, analytical, resourceful, and able to turn incomplete information into practical hypotheses.Willing to work in communities, homes, stores, and installer job sites—not solely from an office.Basic comfort with numbers, customer research, and problem solving.Authorized to work in the United States. International students must have or be able to obtain appropriate CPT/OPT authorization.Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy, Mechanical Engineering, Business, Marketing, Entrepreneurship, Product Management, Business Analytics, Sociology/Anthropology, or a related field. All majors are welcome. Preferred QualificationsInterest in clean energy, home energy systems, consumer products, or local business development.Experience with customer interviews, community engagement, sales, business development, research, or entrepreneurship.Familiarity with home electrical systems, solar, batteries, or backup power is helpful but not required. Career Growth & What You’ll Gain This internship is designed as a launchpad for high-potential talent—not simply a short-term research assignment. Interns will work close to real customers, local partners, and Renogy’s product and business teams, gaining firsthand exposure to how a new energy solution is discovered, defined, validated, and brought to market.High-performing interns may have the opportunity to continue their career with Renogy after the program. Potential next steps are not limited to a market research role and may include opportunities across:Product Development and Product Management, including helping define customer needs, product requirements, and future product roadmaps;Go-to-Market and Product Marketing, including messaging, positioning, launch planning, and market-entry strategy;Market Development and Business Development, including local channel development and strategic partnerships;Sales and Channel Management, including working with installers, retailers, and other distribution partners;Customer Insights and Market Strategy, turning real-world user evidence into business and investment decisions.Top interns may also be invited to contribute to the product-definition and product-launch process, working with cross-functional teams in the United States and China. This is an opportunity to build a broad foundation across product, market, customer, and commercial functions while helping shape the future of home energy solutions.We are looking for individuals who want to do more than complete an internship—we are looking for future builders, product thinkers, market leaders, and business owners. How to ApplyPlease submit your resume and a brief response to the following questions:Why are you interested in home energy, customer discovery, or market exploration?Are you comfortable with cold calling, in-person outreach, and field research?What are your available start/end dates and weekly availability? Renogy is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and evaluate candidates based on qualifications, experience, and job-related skills.

jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 09/06/2026 SummaryAmerican Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with the National Park Service, is seeking one member to contribute to archival projects alongside NPS Staff.About Build Up Technical Internship Program: This position is part of the Build Up Technical Internship Program facilitated by the Historic Preservation Training Center. The Build Up Technical Internship Program is working to expand and diversify the National Park Service workforce while addressing critical maintenance needs by providing professional experiences in technical fields to students and recent graduates.For more information about the Build Up Technical Internship Program, please visit the NPS website.For more information about ACE, please visit our website.Start Date: October 2026Estimated End Date: February 2027*A 16 week minimum commitment is required **This position may be eligible for extension beyond 16 weeks*Location Details/Description The National Parks of Boston encompass a collection of historic, cultural, and coastal park sites located throughout the city of Boston and Boston Harbor. These parks preserve and interpret key locations central to the founding and development of the United States, including sites along the Freedom Trail and the Boston Harbor Islands. The park unit includes historic buildings, landscapes, waterfront resources, and urban green spaces that connect visitors to the nation's history within a vibrant city setting. Scenic views of Boston Harbor, historic neighborhoods, and waterfront areas provide opportunities for recreation, reflection, and learning.For more information about the National Parks of Boston, please visit the NPS website.Position Overview:This member will assist the National Parks of Boston by supporting archival, records management, and cultural resource documentation efforts across multiple park sites. The work supports the National Park Service mission to conserve unimpaired the natural and cultural resources of the National Park System for the enjoyment, education, and inspiration of this and future generations.Archival materials may include historic building documentation, architectural drawings, project files, photographs, maps, planning and construction records, and cultural landscape documentation related to significant sites such as Faneuil Hall, the Charlestown Navy Yard, historic wharves, visitor centers, waterfront infrastructure, trails, walkways, and landscape rehabilitation projects throughout the park unit.The Build Up member will assist with all stages of archival and documentation work, beginning with records appraisal and organization and continuing through description, digitization support, and preparation of materials for long-term preservation and access. Responsibilities may include organizing physical and digital records, applying archival standards and best practices, creating or updating inventories and finding aids, and supporting reference or research requests related to park planning and preservation projects.Schedule: 8:00 AM - 4:30 PM M-FPosition BenefitsLiving Allowance: The ACE Member is expected to contribute ~40 hours/week and will receive a living allowance of $750/week to offset the costs of food and incidental expenses, dispersed bi-weekly.Public Land Corps Hiring Authority: Members serving under this agreement may be eligible for a federal hiring authority upon completion of their term of service and 640 hours of service. If the duration of a PLC-eligible term is not long enough for Members to accrue 640 hours of service (~16 weeks), the total hours served at the completion of the term may be eligible to be combined with hours accrued from another PLC-eligible term to meet the 640 hours requirement. PLC projects also include specific eligibility requirements such as age and citizenship. Please contact ACE staff with questions about eligibility, or view general eligibility information on our website.Housing: Housing is the responsibility of the member and not provided by ACE or the National Park Service. A $250/week housing reimbursement will be provided.Professional Development: The member will have access to up to $1,000 to be used for eligible professional development expenses. Expenses must be approved by the NPS and ACE.Provided Training/Orientation: ACE members will receive position specific training and an orientation outlining ACE policies and procedures, clear guidance on prohibited activities, and networks for support. Specific training may include federal resume-building.QualificationsRequired:Members must be a U.S. citizen or Permanent Resident, as required by U.S. government contractsWilling and able to represent ACE and the partner organization in a professional, positive, and enthusiastic manner.Ability to be both self-directed/work alone, and be a positive, contributing member of a group.A valid driver's license and an insurable driving record (documentation to be provided upon request).Willing to undergo and must pass the required criminal history checksAbility to perform the essential duties of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.ACE Members will need to complete bi-weekly timesheets, beginning of term feedback forms, end of term evaluations and for longer terms, a mid-term evaluation.Member may not participate in any prohibited activities as listed in the Member Service Agreement.To learn more about eligibility requirements, please visit our website.Preferred:Competitive applicants for this position can hold or be pursuing a minimum of a Bachelor's degree in archival work and/or have relevant experience in the subjectAbility and willingness to work as part of a team, and be independently motivated.Deep interest in the National Park Service and archival work.Physical Demands, Work Environment and Working Conditions:Physical Demands: Requires frequent sitting, standing, walking, hiking, carrying, using hands to handle or feel, reaching with hands and arms, talking and hearing. Manual dexterity required for use of various tools, computer keyboard/mouse and other office equipment. Required to stoop, kneel, climb stairs, and/or crouch. Ability to hike over rough terrain.Vision Requirements: Requires close, distance, peripheral and depth perception vision as well as the ability to focus.Weight Lifted or Force Exerted: Frequently moves up to 10 lbs., ability to move up to 50 pounds.Environmental: Outdoor and indoor conditions. Work environment conditions can change frequently; working under adverse weather conditions and in various climates. Mainly indoor, office environment conditions; indoor air quality is good and temperature is controlled.Noise Environment: Moderate to high noise such as gas-powered chainsaws and other hand and power tools. Moderate noise such as in a business office with equipment and light traffic.Travel: This position may require domestic travel.Environmental Conditions/Hazards: The ACE member(s) may encounter environmental conditions/hazards including extreme heat or cold, rocky terrain, swamp or wetland conditions, biting insects, and potentially dangerous wildlife. The member is expected to conduct duties in a safe and orderly manner so as not to endanger self, fellow staff/members or resources.Vehicle and Equipment Use/Safety: If a vehicle is required for the accomplishment of the duties, one will be provided by the NPS or ACE. Any tools required for the accomplishment of the duties will be provided by the NPS. Use of personal protective equipment (PPE), typically provided by the NPS, will be mandatory for any activity that requires it. Strict adherence to NPS and ACE equipment training, certification and safety protocols is required.To Apply: Please submit your resume, a cover letter demonstrating your interest and experience, and contact information for three professional/academic references to the online application page for this position on usa conservation website. Support fundraising prep, investor updates, metrics snapshots, financial summaries, market research, and strategic narratives.Operating dashboards. Build dashboards that help the team understand what is working, what is broken, and what needs attention.Market research. Study AI startups, company-building platforms, agent products, vertical SaaS, consumer/prosumer tools, and startup tooling markets.Unit economics. Help analyze CAC, payback, LTV, gross margin, infrastructure costs, model costs, support costs, and customer profitability.Decision support. Work with founders and team leads to turn data into decisions around hiring, product roadmap, GTM, pricing, and capital allocation.Shipping velocity. This is not fake analyst work. You will work on real numbers, real company decisions, real investor materials, and real operating systems.What We Are Looking ForYou are strong with numbers. You can work in spreadsheets, build models, analyze data, and explain what matters.You care about startups, not just finance. You want to understand how a company actually gets built.You are analytical but practical. You do not just make beautiful models. You help people make better decisions.You are comfortable with ambiguity. Early-stage startup data is messy. Your job is to create clarity.You have high agency. You do not wait around for permission.You communicate clearly. You can summarize a model, explain a metric, write an investor update, or turn messy data into a simple recommendation.You are unusually good at something. Maybe you invest personally, built a startup model, ran finance for a club, analyzed companies for fun, worked on a fund, built dashboards, or obsessed over how great companies grow.BonusYou have experience with startups, venture capital, investment banking, private equity, consulting, accounting, FP&A, or business operations.You have built financial models for startups before.You understand SaaS metrics, AI infrastructure costs, usage-based pricing, or marketplace economics.You are comfortable with Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, Python, Notion, Airtable, or BI tools.You follow AI companies, venture markets, startup funding, and technology trends.You are good at making complicated numbers feel simple.How We WorkWe work five to six days a week at the office.We move fast, talk to users constantly, ship aggressively, and care about making Skarmy feel magical.We go out, decompress, and are human. We really love concerts, KBBQs, founder dinners, and strange experiments.The rest of the time, we are building.By applying, you agree to sign up for the Skarmy.

jobs.description: Employer: Palmetto Bluff Expires: 09/07/2026 Summary:Palmetto Bluff is nestled along the May River in the Lowcountry of South Carolina between Hilton Head Island and Savannah. As an award winning 20,000-acre development, the development encompasses a private member’s only club which includes a marina, restaurants, an equestrian center, a shooting club, a Jack Nicklaus Signature Golf Course, a King-Collins 9-Hole Course, lawn and racquet club, and more. In addition, Palmetto Bluff has an extensive nature preserve, walking trails, retail shopping, and a vibrant village, all which pay homage to the region’s rich heritage.Palmetto Bluff’s Culinary and Baking and Pastry Externships are designed to provide qualified culinary students with the tools necessary to succeed in this very competitive industry. By working alongside Palmetto Bluff chefs, managers and staff, student externs gain practical experience and insight into all aspects of Club operations, from lavish weddings and private parties to state-of-the-art restaurants. The four restaurant concepts within the Club range from casual dining to the finest restaurants in the region. Ultimately, student externships at the Palmetto Bluff are a fantastic way for career-minded hospitality students to satisfy academic requirements while gaining valuable, resume-building work experience, building professional relationships and enhancing their interpersonal and professional skills.In return, Palmetto Bluff benefits from the energy, vitality, and fresh perspective externs bring to our operation. And, because many of our best employees started their careers as externs, it is an ideal way to include more students and recent graduates into our growing professional network!About the Externships:Culinary and Baking and Pastry Externs are assigned to one of the following popular Club facilities:Cole’s/CanteenMay River GrillCanoe Club Venue assignments depend on business requirements as well as previous work experience, qualifications, and externship objectives. Because each venue has its own distinctive style and traditions, no two externships will be exactly alike. All students may reasonably expect to participate in every aspect of Club operations during their externship experience. All externs will contribute individually and as a team to support goals and objectives assigned by experienced culinary mentors and each student will benefit from on the job training and continued mentoring in their specialized field of study. Externs must be passionate about the culinary industry, have a positive attitude and a love for learning. Palmetto Bluff is an exciting and fast paced environment where initiative and enthusiasm are rewarded!Learning Objectives:Play a vital role in tracking trends, working in state-of-the-art kitchens, and assisting established chefs.Gain specific technical skills and knowledge necessary to excel in a fine-dining, private club environmentContribute to recipe development, test and experiment with new ideas and concepts, and understand the effect of menu training on the overall quality of serviceDiscover effective tactics to motivate staff and inspire teamwork and cooperation. Gain practical, resume-building work experience at a top tier private clubBuild strong relationships with Palmetto Bluff staff and managers and expand your professional network by connecting with leaders in the culinary and hospitality industry.Gain valuable knowledge regarding growing cycle of produce and peak times to grow and harvest a wide variety of produce.About the Restaurants:Located within the Moreland Clubhouse, Cole’s featuring local farmers, fishermen, and purveyors, Cole’s Lowcountry Tavern is a family-friendly member’s meeting place where local produce is paired with innovative libations, local brews, curated wines, and friendly service. Cole’s lounge features several TVs, 17 bar seats and assorted lounge seating. Enjoy a draft beer or a signature Cole’s cocktail at the bar or on the screened porch overlooking the marsh.The Canteen is the perfect spot in Moreland Village to pick up a cup of coffee or breakfast sandwich in the morning and a homemade panini, a wrap, a salad or snacks in the afternoon. Take it to go or enjoy an afternoon on the Canteen’s open-air porch with a glass of wine or a beer from a local brewery.Nestled alongside the pristine fairways and stunning live oaks of the May River Golf Course, the May River Grill at the clubhouse is the ideal spot for casual dining or a relaxing post-round meal. Enjoy lunch indoors or check out the action on the links on the outdoor terrace. Fancy a drink? Enjoy an enticing cocktail at the bar while watching golfers finish their round on the 18th green. May River Grill serves lunch to members and Inn guests with scheduled tee times and provides drinks and refreshing cocktails until the last player finishes.The Canoe Club is all about Southern comfort. Enjoy dining with panoramic views of the May River on one side and the Palmetto Bluff inland waterway on the other. Our “coastal kitchen” menu celebrates local seafood, drawing ingredients and inspiration from the May River with staples including local shrimp, oysters and seafood prepared in a variety of ways. By partnering with area farms, we are able to source fresh vegetables, beef and poultry to create dishes that honor the bounty of the South Carolina Lowcountry.To deliver on something that aspires to do more than serve as a farm, we use the Palmetto Bluff Farm to lead the way in recapturing and cultivating authentic farming practices of the Lowcountry of South Carolina and celebrate and collaborate with the farmers, hunters, fishermen and craftsmen who share our vision.Schedules:Externs work full time schedules (35-40+ hours per week 5-6 days per week). Extern start dates can be somewhat flexible but are generally mid-January for Spring externs, mid-May for Summer externs, and mid-September for Fall externs. Externships last 14-20 consecutive weeks.Pay Rates:ALL externships are PAID. Total compensation per hour is $15 + 4% Food and Beverage Commission. The Club also provides daily, chef-prepared meals for all employees!Housing and TransportationThe Employee Hotel is location is approximately 30 minutes from the Club in an excellent location in Bluffton just between Hilton Head Island and Downtown Bluffton minutes from the beaches. The cost of housing is $125/week for a single room or $50/week for a shared room(double occupancy) which includes all utilities and is deducted from paychecks biweekly ($250 or $100 deducted per paycheck). Transportation to and from work is also available if needed and parking is complimentary. Requirements:Externs must be currently enrolled in an accredited culinary school or a recent graduate of oneStrong knife skills and basic kitchen knowledge are essentialAt least one year of BOH experience is strongly preferredAbility to work 12-20 consecutive weeksApplications will be accepted on a rolling basis until all positions are filledMust be able to meet the physical requirements of the job (as outlined in the job description)The Bluffton area offers many exciting and interesting things to enjoy during non-working hours including nationally acclaimed restaurants, the beaches on Hilton Head Island and Tybee Island, fishing, shopping, and more. Just a short drive from Beaufort, SC, Savannah, GA and Charleston, SC. If you want to build your resume, learn from award-winning chefs, work hard AND have fun, apply for a Palmetto Bluff Externship today by emailing your resume!
